title: Size-4 Counterexamples to the Sidon-Extension Conjecture
summary: A finite set $S \subset \mathbb{Z}$ is a Sidon set if its pairwise differences are distinct. Recall that a perfect difference set (PDS) of order $n$ is a set $B \subset \mathbb{Z}_v$ ($v = n^2 - n + 1$) of size $n$ such that every nonzero residue arises exactly once as a difference of two elements of $B$.
